feed.title: Launch Desk
feed.subtitle: Sample data: a fictional outlet (Product launches and business news).

entry.title: Corvid launches the RV-90 graphics card
entry.content:
Corvid has launched the RV-90, its new flagship graphics card. The card will cost $899. It goes on sale December 10.

Under the hood is Nocturne, the company's new graphics architecture. The card carries 24 GB of GDDR7 memory. Corvid claims the RV-90 doubles the RV-80's ray-tracing performance.

entry.title: Meridian cable damage slows internet in six countries
entry.content:
The Meridian undersea cable was damaged on Saturday. Talvera Networks leads the group of carriers that owns it.

Talvera expects repairs to take about three weeks. The repair ship Vela Constance is due at the site on November 20.

Until then, the carriers that depend on Meridian have a slow few weeks ahead.

entry.title: Orbelle launches 40 more internet satellites
entry.content:
Orbelle put 40 more internet satellites into orbit overnight. Service starts in mid-2027. It will cost $89 a month.

The company has raised $2.3 billion so far. It needs 1,200 satellites in orbit by March 2030 to keep its spectrum license. That's a lot of launches, and a lot of money, still to come.

entry.title: Ferngrove cuts 2,000 jobs
entry.content:
Ferngrove is cutting 2,000 jobs. That's about 4% of its workforce.

Most of the cuts land on Hearth, the company's smart home division. That says a lot about where Ferngrove now sees its future.

Ferngrove expects to book $310 million in charges, most of it for severance. The costs arrive right away. The savings will take longer to show up.

Investors will want to hear what Ferngrove plans to do with the money it saves, and whether more cuts are coming.

entry.title: Wayline starts paid robotaxi rides in Port Ellery
entry.content:
Wayline has started paid robotaxi service in Port Ellery. Fares are $3 to start plus $1.90 per mile. The launch fleet is 40 cars.

Wayline plans to grow that to 200 cars by mid-2027. The company raised $600 million in September. It pays the city 25 cents for every ride.

That's a lot of rides to make the math work.

entry.title: Thrushwell unveils the Pulse 4 smartwatch
entry.content:
Thrushwell has unveiled the Pulse 4, its next smartwatch. It costs $299. It ships December 3.

Thrushwell says the battery lasts up to four days on a charge. That's the number Thrushwell wants buyers to remember. At that price, the Pulse 4 lands in the middle of the premium watch market, where battery life is still the easiest way to stand out.

entry.title: Pixelforge announces the Forge Deck 2
entry.content:
Pixelforge has announced the Forge Deck 2 handheld console. Pricing starts at $549. A model with 1 TB of storage costs $649.

Preorders open November 20. The console reaches stores February 18.

The original Forge Deck drops to $349. Pixelforge says it has sold 6.2 million of them. That's a big base of owners to win back.

entry.title: Ransomware attack hits Marrowfield Health hospital chain
entry.content:
Ransomware struck Marrowfield Health on Friday. The company operates 11 hospitals. It reported $3.4 billion in revenue last year.

The attackers want $8 million. Marrowfield Health has postponed elective surgeries through Tuesday.

Every cancelled surgery costs money, and so does every day the systems stay down. The bigger bill may still be ahead.

entry.title: Judge rules against Ferngrove's app store rules
entry.content:
A judge has found that Ferngrove's Canopy app store rules broke antitrust law. The money at stake is large.

Ferngrove's standard cut of in-app purchases is 30%. Canopy brought in $11.4 billion in commissions last year.

Ferngrove shares fell 5% in afternoon trading after the ruling. Investors can do the math.

entry.title: Tidewell buys messaging app Murmurline for $3.2 billion
entry.content:
Tidewell has agreed to buy the messaging app Murmurline. The price is $3.2 billion. Tidewell is paying entirely in cash, with no stock in the mix.

Murmurline has 85 million monthly users. That's the prize. Messaging is where people spend their time online, and Tidewell wants more of that time.

The companies expect the deal to close by mid-2027. That's a long runway, and a lot can change before any money moves. Expect hard questions along the way, and a few nervous users.

entry.title: Nimbusfold outage knocks apps and sites offline for hours
entry.content:
Apps and websites went dark for hours Friday when Nimbusfold's cloud failed. Delivery app Tinbowl and online bank Brassmint were among the casualties.

Everything was back up by 08:25 UTC. It was a rough morning for anyone who rents servers from Nimbusfold. Expect questions about who pays for the lost orders.

entry.title: Lumora launches the Arc 7 phone
entry.content:
Lumora has launched the Arc 7, its latest flagship phone. It costs $799. Sales start November 20.

The phone will be sold in 14 countries at launch. Inside is the Facet 3, Lumora's newest in-house chip.

At that price, the Arc 7 goes straight at the year's other big flagships, and the new chip will have to carry the pitch.

entry.title: Kestrel Aerial cleared for drone deliveries
entry.content:
Kestrel Aerial is cleared to start drone deliveries. The first orders fly on December 1.

Each delivery will cost customers $3.99. Grocery chain Pantryfield is Kestrel's first retail partner.

Kestrel raised $180 million from investors in May. Now it has to show that a drone can beat a delivery van on cost.

entry.title: Ampwright Labs shows solid-state battery cells for phones
entry.content:
Ampwright Labs has shown solid-state battery cells for phones. The startup also announced $310 million in new funding. The round values it at $2.1 billion.

Ampwright will open a pilot production line in 2027. Mass production is planned for 2028.

That's an aggressive timeline for a technology known for slipping, and investors will be watching the pilot line closely.

entry.title: Sable Labs launches its Sable 4 AI model
entry.content:
Sable Labs has launched Sable 4, the latest version of its AI model. Developers pay $1.20 per million input tokens to use it through the API.

The two smaller versions, with 8 billion and 32 billion parameters, cost nothing to download. That's aggressive pricing for a model this capable, and rivals will have to answer it.

entry.title: Brightmesh rushes out a patch for its router takeover flaw
entry.content:
Brightmesh is scrambling after a flaw let attackers hijack its home routers. Firmware 4.2.1, out now, closes the hole.

Three older models won't get the fix. Brightmesh says it will replace those routers for free.

Brightmesh shares fell 6% in early trading. Free replacements cost money, but losing customers' trust would cost more.

entry.title: TicketRiver breach hits 9 million accounts
entry.content:
TicketRiver says a breach exposed 9 million customer accounts.

The company will pay for 2 years of credit monitoring for affected customers. TicketRiver shares fell 9% in afternoon trading.

The timing could hardly be worse. Cleanup bills come next, and they won't be small, but winning back nervous buyers may cost even more.

entry.title: Gloamstream raises streaming prices
entry.content:
Gloamstream is raising prices on all three of its streaming plans.

The ad-supported plan goes from $7.99 to $8.99 a month. Standard rises from $13.99 to $15.99. Premium climbs from $19.99 to $22.99.

Current subscribers will pay the new prices from December 12.

Premium takes the biggest jump. The message is clear: Gloamstream wants more money from its most committed customers, and it's betting few of them will leave over a few dollars. Watch the cancellation numbers next quarter to see whether that bet holds.

entry.title: Ferrolith to build a $14 billion chip plant in Ashford Flats
entry.content:
Memory chipmaker Ferrolith will build a chip plant in Ashford Flats, Texas. The price tag: $14 billion.

Construction starts in March 2027. Production is set to begin in 2029. That's a long runway, and memory prices will rise and fall more than once before the first wafer leaves the building.

Once it's running at full speed, the plant will employ 2,200 people. For Ashford Flats, the jobs are the headline. For Ferrolith, the bet is that demand for memory will still be there when the plant is ready.

entry.title: Tallow DB switches to a source-available license
entry.content:
Tallow DB is switching to a source-available license. Cloud companies will need a paid deal to offer it as a service.

The company behind it, Tallow DB Inc., says rival cloud hosts were undercutting its own hosted service. That service, Tallow DB Cloud, brings in 70% of the company's revenue.

The company raised $95 million in July. Follow the money, and the license change makes sense.

entry.title: Quarrow Motors recalls 80,000 electric cars over software flaw
entry.content:
Quarrow Motors is recalling 80,000 of its electric cars. The fix is a free over-the-air update. Roughly 6,000 cars will have to visit a dealer instead.

Quarrow expects the recall to cost about $9 million. That's small money for a carmaker, but recalls rarely help sales. Investors will be watching December deliveries.

entry.title: Aurelith launches the Visor mixed-reality headset
entry.content:
Aurelith launched the Visor on Monday, its first mixed-reality headset. The Visor costs $1,499. It ships December 4.

At launch, it will only be sold in the US and Canada. The headset weighs 545 g.

That's a premium price for a first-generation product from a company that has never sold a headset. Aurelith is pitching comfort over raw specs, a bet aimed at people who tried a headset once and put it back in the box. The next few weeks of reviews will show whether that bet pays off.

entry.title: Note-taking startup Quillnest raises $6 million
entry.content:
Note-taking startup Quillnest has raised $6 million in seed funding. Larkhollow Partners led the round.

Quillnest's app turns meeting notes into task lists without sending them to a server, because everything runs on the user's own device. The company says it has 140,000 monthly users, up from 30,000 in March.

The money goes to hiring. Quillnest plans to grow from 9 employees to 25 by the end of 2027. A paid team plan arrives in the spring at $8 per user per month.

Co-founders Mara Lindqvist and Jonah Petrakis started the company in 2024. Privacy is the pitch, and so far it's working.
